item.description:
## New
- **Scratch That** (opt-in): dictation now resolves spoken self-corrections — "make the padding 20 pixels, scratch that, 8 pixels" comes out as "make the padding 8 pixels". Understands cues like "no wait", "I mean", "changed my mind", and "start over". While you speak, the corrected-away words are struck through live in the popover, then swept away. Fully on-device: a built-in heuristic everywhere, with Apple's on-device model handling trickier phrasing when Apple Intelligence is available. Enable it in Settings → Prompt → "Fix self-corrections".
## Fixed
- A slow transcript finalization could bleed a previous dictation into your next recording — re-freezing old text into the popover, auto-copying a half-finished session, and clearing the live one. Late results now never interrupt a newer session, and cleared prompts stay cleared (the text remains available in capture history) - Auto-paste could land inside Relay's own Settings window when it still had keyboard focus — including into a dictionary rule's replacement field, silently corrupting the rule. Relay now verifies the focused field belongs to another app before pasting; otherwise the prompt simply stays on the clipboard

## New
- **LLM output history** — the History section now has a Captures / LLM output toggle. Every composed prompt that leaves Relay (copied or auto-pasted) is kept, newest first; click one to copy it back, and each row shows the app it went to
## Fixed
- **Menu bar clicks are instant again** — macOS's focus protection was flagging Relay as a "key thief" for grabbing key window status without activating, and quietly delayed clicks by up to a second (or dropped them). Relay now activates properly when the popover opens and hands focus back to the app you were in when it closes - Clicking the icon to close the popover no longer occasionally closes-and-instantly-reopens it, which read as a dead click - The menu bar icon no longer blinks its highlight for a frame when the popover opens, and the held highlight can't get stuck after rapid open/close

## New
- **AI Polish** — on-device transcript cleanup with Apple's Foundation Models: fixes punctuation and drops filler words, right from the transcript menu (macOS 26+) - **Custom dictionary** — define word removals and replacements that apply to every transcript - **Vocabulary boosting** — add terms (names, jargon) that all speech engines are biased toward recognizing - **Correction learning (opt-in)** — after auto-paste, Relay learns vocabulary from the words you fix by hand; entirely on-device - **Apple SpeechAnalyzer engine** — a fourth speech engine on macOS 26+ - **Recording sounds** — start/stop sounds with selectable themes, including the ambient Felt, Ripple, and Halo family (turn off in settings) - **Auto-stop on silence (opt-in)** — dictation stops itself after an adjustable stretch of silence - **Duck system audio while recording (opt-in)** — music fades down while you dictate - **Warm capture (opt-in)** — keeps the mic warm so recordings include ~0.45s from before the hotkey landed; no more clipped first words - **Faster first dictation** — downloaded speech models prewarm on launch, wake, and unlock - **Bundled MCP server** — the Claude Code bridge now ships inside the app as a native Swift server; no Node install needed - **Input device follows the system default** — switch your mic in System Settings, Raycast, or by connecting AirPods and Relay follows, even mid-recording - **Paste last transcript** — re-paste your most recent dictation without re-recording - Capture history now persists across restarts and updates, and shows the app each capture came from - Settings polish: explanatory tooltips, reorganized sections, cleaner pickers
## Fixed
- Capturing from a specific mic no longer changes your system-wide input device (new low-level audio capture layer) - Mics muted at the hardware level are unmuted automatically before recording instead of producing silent transcripts - Very short recordings no longer come back empty on the Parakeet engine - Auto-paste is more reliable: waits for the paste to commit, and only restores your clipboard if nothing else changed it - The menu bar icon stays highlighted while the panel is open

## New
- **Screenshots auto-added while recording** — captures land in your stack automatically, no need to know about ⌃-to-clipboard (works with CleanShot and custom save locations) - **Recent captures history** — the last 20 captures in settings, one click to copy any of them back - **Right-click the menu bar icon** to jump straight to settings - **Popover closes after copying** (turn off in Behavior settings) - **Dock controls** — start/stop recording from the Dock menu; clicking the Dock icon opens the panel - **Custom annotation cursor** while drawing on screen
## Fixed
- The end of your dictation no longer gets cut off when transcription takes a moment to finalize - Pressing Esc to cancel a recording no longer closes dialogs in the app you're working in - Claude Code's MCP bridge now sees live state during recording

## New
- Launch at login - Show in Dock (opt-in) - Start recording on menu bar click (opt-in) - Hold ⇧ to send after paste (opt-in)
## Fixes
- Auto-paste to focused input now works reliably — text is inserted directly via the Accessibility API with ⌘V as fallback, into the app you were working in - Permission prompts for accessibility and event posting instead of silent failures

## New
- Notarized with Apple Developer ID — no more Gatekeeper warnings - Custom clipboard overlay icon
## Fixes
- Accessibility status refreshes when opening settings

## New
- Context-aware filler word removal — "like" and "right" are cleaned when used as fillers while preserved when meaningful (e.g. "I like this", "looks like a bug") - Pin popover — keep the popover open when clicking outside
## Fixes
- Filter empty voice notes from composed output - Fix accessibility dialog loop and add not-granted banner
